children: rose 3.3% in after-hours trading amid a report that activist investor Barington Capital has taken a stake and wants the retailer to explore a sale.

“We believe changes are needed at this company,” Barington CEO James Mitarotonda said in an interview with Bloomberg. “Given the market leadership nature of the company, the brand value, and the cash flow, there should be considerable interest.”
Mitarotonda said the company would likely see strong interest from private equity firms. Barington, which owns about 1 million Bath & Body
shares, wants the company to increase its revenue and repurchase shares. Barington plans to publish a letter to BBWI's board in the coming weeks and is looking into potential board representation.
Barington led a campaign against the company in 2019, when it was named L Brands.
Bath & Body Works told Bloomberg the company regularly engages with shareholders and values their perspectives.

“Our board and management team regularly evaluate opportunities to enhance shareholder value and will continue to make decisions in the best long-term interests of the company and its shareholders,” they said in a statement.

title: Bath & Body Works gains on report activist  Barington takes stake, pushes for sale
